So I was playing a video game and I thought it was a bit strange how a frag grenade had roughly the same explosion radius as a mini nuke. In real life, would a stronger explosion also have to have a large explosion radius?

According to TV shows, there are different types of explosives used for "soft" or "hard" targets (people vs buildings and machinery). Does that factor into the main question?
Does a stronger explosion always = bigger radius?

Generally explosions of the same amount of energy do the same damage. But humans are more vulnerable to metal than to air, so frag grenades, antiperson mines and terrorist bombs have metal pieces around the explosive.

To do most damage to a soft target (i.e.hunting) it needs a soft bullet which gets deformed and therefore creates a funnel shaped wound. Against hard targets bullets harder than the armor of the target are used, these aren't designed to deform, but to keep the shape and penetrate.
